defects.description: The shift condition uses `insert_value > collection[insert_index - 1]`, which shifts while the value is larger and yields a descending order; ascending insertion sort needs `<`.
paraphrases: The comparison should be `<`, not `>`; as written it sorts descending.
Shifting while the value is greater reverses the sort order.
insertion_sort([0,5,3,2,2]) would not come out ascending with `>`.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `insert_value < collection[insert_index - 1]`. Real (wrong order), findable via the ascending docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The outer loop `range(1, len(collection) - 1)` stops before the last element, so the final element is never inserted and the list is left partially unsorted.
paraphrases: `range(1, len(collection) - 1)` should be `range(1, len(collection))`; the last element is skipped.
The loop stops one short, leaving the final item unsorted.
Off-by-one in the outer range drops the last insertion.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `range(1, len(collection))`. Real (last element not sorted), findable via the docstring examples, distinct.

defects.description: The shift `collection[insert_index] = collection[insert_index]` assigns the element to itself instead of copying the previous element down (`collection[insert_index - 1]`), so nothing is shifted and values are overwritten.
paraphrases: The right-hand side should be `collection[insert_index - 1]`; the shift is a no-op.
Assigning the slot to itself copies nothing down, so the insert overwrites data.
The element to the left is never moved into place.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `collection[insert_index] = collection[insert_index - 1]`. Real (shift does nothing / data loss), findable by reading the assignment, distinct.
